retained_skill: Identify which image pixels and RGB least-significant bits carry the payload, assemble those bits in the correct order, and decode the hidden ASCII flag.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts first encounter a broken advertised tool setup, then search many channel, order, offset, and traversal combinations without identifying the alternating-pixel carrier; 10 of 12 end at a context or time limit and the two submissions contain guesses rather than the extracted payload.
change: Repair the environment so the default python3 can import Pillow, correct the false image-size description, and structurally shrink the carrier from 32x32 to 16x8 while preserving the same secret and alternating-pixel RGB-LSB scheme. The help is in the original image signal made easier to reach: it removes 87.5% of carrier pixels and leaves exactly one payload-sized set of alternating pixels, so students still must infer pixel selection and perform LSB extraction but need far fewer traversal experiments.
restore: Restore the original 32x32 carrier after the student learns to recognize and test the alternating-pixel signal; keep the repaired default Python/Pillow setup and truthful size wording.
prediction: The change addresses repeated exhaustive traversal searches after ordinary all-pixel LSB decoding produces noise. With only 128 pixels and a payload-sized alternating subset, some attempts will test that subset and decode printable ASCII before exhausting their budget; this is refuted if attempts use working Pillow promptly but still spend their remaining turns trying unrelated transforms without testing alternating pixels, or test alternating pixels and do not recover the flag.
